reason: I want to harvest lettuce for the garden meal; scissors are a natural way to cut leaves.
expectation: I expect to get lettuce leaves ready for washing or eating.

alternatives.reason: Water might help the lettuce, but harvesting directly serves the meal goal.

effect: The harvest produced leaves as expected, so I can prepare them for the meal.
reaction: A straightforward, reassuring harvest; the storm label connects it to the setting.
reason: Washing the harvested lettuce with drinking water seems like the next food preparation step.
expectation: I expect clean lettuce to combine with the ration or eat.

alternatives.reason: Watering the trough could support it, but the meal is the immediate goal.

effect: The leaves are washed, so they can be added to the warm ration.
reaction: This is predictable food preparation, with little new to discover so far.
reason: Adding the washed leaves to the ration should make the garden meal.
expectation: I expect a meal and completion of the eating goal.

effect: The supper completes the goal and brings the garden and protected discovery together in the storm scene.
reaction: The two fans and covered window make the quiet survival feel tangible; I liked that payoff.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making supper gave the earlier work protecting the plants and core a quiet human payoff; the two fans made it vivid.

leastWorthwhile.text: Washing the lettuce felt routine and repeated the earlier harvest preparation without adding much discovery.

surprise.text: The meal passage shifted attention to the two fans protecting both roots and core; the practical details made their shared vulnerability clearer.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless: harvesting, washing and adding leaves to a ration follow naturally, though they offered little challenge.

continue.text: Yes, I would continue to see how the storm ends and what happens to the discovery, although this chapter's choices alone were fairly predictable.
